messages.text: Moved here from T-002 (04:00 +07). Status: the panel slide-in fix landed (b43443b). Your finger check: better than before, but still a bit laggy. Next: the first frame of the slide-in still does 2 extra layouts, cause not found yet. fix-scroll-engine looks for it on the Simulator, then one phone check to confirm. Results come here.

Simulator result (04:08 +07, 2 runs, OBSERVED, matches your phone): the panel's first slide-in costs about 19-20 ms of style work with 2 extra whole-page layouts; the second slide-in in the same visit costs about 2 ms. So it's a one-time setup cost. New suspect: on the first slide-in the panel switches from 'inactive' to active, which makes Safari restyle the whole panel, and it starts loading its images. Next run: switch the panel to active before you reach it, to see whether the first frame becomes as cheap as the second.

Update (04:12 +07, Simulator): activating the panel early did not help: the first slide-in still costs 18-19 ms with 2 extra layouts. One first-time step is left to test: the panel starting to load its images. That run is going now.
Could we test it on the real iphone device ?

Yes. As soon as the Simulator run that's going now finishes (a few minutes), the same test runs on your real iPhone: the robot driver plays the panel slide-in and records Safari's layout records, comparing the current fix with the image-loading step held back. You don't need to touch the phone for it, and no times are compared. Results come here.

Page end update (04:20 +07). Simulator check (OBSERVED): the panel's pictures loading for the first time are not what makes the first slide-in slow. The first slide-in still costs about 20 ms of style work, the second about 2 ms. The Simulator couldn't confirm the block took effect, so the real-iPhone test you asked for now runs. It compares the current fix with and without the picture loads, and checks that the block really worked. I'll post the result here.

Real-iPhone result (04:38 +07, your phone, our own recordings): blocking the panel's picture loads does NOT make the first slide-in cheaper. The block did take effect in every run, so the result is solid.
- First slide-in: about 14-17 ms of style work plus 2 extra page layouts (about 4.4 ms and 1.4 ms), with or without the pictures.
- Second slide-in: 0.2-0.5 ms with no extra layouts.
So the cost is real, it is one-time only, and it isn't the pictures. The phone stayed under 40 °C and both check runs passed.
Next: fix-scroll-engine tests five other 'first time only' causes on the Simulator (fonts, image decoding, the panel's first style calculation, and two CSS ones). Any fix will keep the look identical.
